title: Central and Peripheral Oxygen Distribution in Two Different Modes of Interval Training
population: 24 healthy recreationally active men, 24.3 ± 3.6 years; cardiac output available in 17; not an Ironman cohort
work: Five 3-min work phases versus 30 short work phases of 30 s, arranged in five 6-min sections; matched work rate and time
recovery: Long condition: each complete section has 3 min work and 3 min active recovery. Short condition starts with 30 s active recovery to align work-phase sampling. This does not settle a TFCL source's missing final rest.
frequency: Three experimental visits within two weeks, at least 48 h apart; acute protocols, not a weekly training prescription
limits: Recreational males; acute mechanistic contrast; equal work rates; not an individual optimum, not FTP-based prescription

title: Aerobic  high‐intensity  intervals are superior to improve V̇O 2max  compared with sprint intervals in  well‐trained  men
population: 48 aerobically well-trained healthy men randomized; 31 analyzed (10 HIIT, 12 short-rest SIT, 9 long-rest SIT); accustomed to treadmill but not specialized competitive runners
work: HIIT 4×4 min compared with approximately 8×20 s exhaustive running and 10×30 s maximal running; treadmill approximately 3 degrees
recovery: Three 3-min active recoveries between the four work bouts; a separately stated final 3-min cool-down at the same 70% HRmax intensity
frequency: 3 sessions/week for 8 weeks; other high-intensity endurance prohibited during intervention; other usual physical activities allowed
limits: Male selected sample, no direct bike transfer, protocol-specific training volume, no individual TFCL dose established; some SIT intolerance reported

title: Low cadence interval training at moderate intensity does not improve cycling performance in highly trained veteran cyclists
population: 22 well-trained male veteran cyclists randomized, age 47 ± 6; low-cadence group 11, reported training-diary control 10; strength outcomes only 7/9; table sample labels require caution
work: 5×6 min at 40 rpm versus added freely chosen cadence moderate cycling
recovery: Methods say 3-min active rest in-between 5 efforts, but also report 30 min active rest weekly across two sessions: 24 min if strictly n−1 versus reported 30. Do not choose the missing final rest to reconcile the paper.
frequency: 2 sessions/week for 12 weeks in addition to usual training; freely chosen cadence group adds 90 min moderate cycling weekly
limits: Veteran male sample; cadence, HR anchors and duration differ; internal recovery-volume ambiguity; prior training history incompletely known; subgroup strength tests

title: Effects of Passive or Active Recovery Regimes Applied During Long-Term Interval Training on Physical Fitness in Healthy Trained and Untrained Individuals: A Systematic Review
population: 24 included studies; 501 participants in active-recovery programs and 229 in passive-recovery programs; trained/untrained, 14–48 years
work: Heterogeneous interval-training programs, 3–15 weeks; no single common workout prescription
recovery: Active/passive during repeated efforts or sets; does not test presence of an undocumented final rest in TFCL recipes
frequency: Heterogeneous trial frequencies and durations; no universal schedule inferred
limits: Heterogeneous populations, interventions and outcomes; primarily separate programs rather than uniform head-to-head comparison; no final-rest rule

title: Discomfort, pain and fatigue levels of 160 cyclists after a kinematic bike-fitting method: an experimental study
population: 160 adult amateur mountain-bike cyclists, 120 men and 40 women; no randomized control group; recreational/competitive mix
work: 120-s fitting observations at 100 W and 70–90 rpm, adjustments until at least 15 of 18 kinematic measurements in manufacturer reference ranges; not an aero interval workout
recovery: Subjects dismount and rest while adjustments are made; no training recovery duration or final-rest count specified
frequency: One fitting intervention, usual mileage maintained, subjective scales repeated after 30 days
limits: Mountain-bike population, uncontrolled design, subjective outcomes, no long aero-position tolerance or interval dose tested
